## Walkthrough

Introduced a module-scoped cache for WASM module compilation to reuse the compiled module across multiple invocations. Added a public `getWasmBytes()` function to expose raw WASM bytes. Updated the package version from 1.1.1 to 1.1.2.

## Changes

| Cohort / File(s) | Summary |
|---|---|
| **WASM Module Caching** <br> `bin/build-inline.ts` | Introduced `compiledModulePromise` cache to compile the WASM module once and reuse across calls; modified `instantiate()` to use cached promise; added new public export `getWasmBytes()` to decode and return raw WASM bytes from base64 string. |
| **Version Update** <br> `package.json` | Updated version from 1.1.1 to 1.1.2. |

## Estimated code review effort

🎯 2 (Simple) | ⏱️ ~8 minutes

- Review the caching pattern implementation for correctness and thread-safety implications in `compiledModulePromise`
- Verify that `getWasmBytes()` correctly decodes base64 and handles potential errors
- Confirm that `instantiate()` properly leverages the cache without introducing unintended side effects

## Possibly related PRs

- **#103**: Modifies `bin/build-inline.ts` instantiate and getWasmBytes exports, directly related to WASM module initialization changes
- **#106**: Alters `bin/build-inline.ts` instantiate/getWasmBytes surface and implementation, modifies how WASM bytes are exposed and instantiation is performed

## Poem

> 🐰 A cache now holds the module dear,  
> No recompilation year after year!  
> Bytes exposed through getWasmBytes' call,  
> One swift compilation to serve them all. ✨

<summary>bin/build-inline.ts (2)</summary><blockquote>

`52-52`: **Excellent optimization with proper lazy initialization.**

The module-scoped cache ensures the WASM module is compiled only once and reused across all subsequent invocations. The implementation correctly leverages JavaScript's single-threaded execution model—the check and assignment on lines 56-57 execute atomically before yielding at the await, preventing any race conditions.

Note: If compilation fails, the rejected promise will be cached, causing all future calls to fail immediately with the same error. This fail-fast behavior is appropriate for invalid WASM bytes.




Also applies to: 56-60

---

`64-66`: **LGTM: Clean helper for accessing raw WASM bytes.**

The `getWasmBytes()` function properly decodes the base64 string and returns a Uint8Array. This is now exposed as a public API (as documented in the generated .d.ts file), allowing external callers to access the raw WASM bytes if needed.
